fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. "A third of the earth was burned up, along with a third of the trees and all the green grass." Hail and fire mixed with blood were hurled down upon the earth first, and then came the burning. I've burned a batch or two myself, but never a third of the earth.

Yes, baker. "A third of the stars were darkened, a third of the day was without light, and a third of the night as well." So a third of the day goes without light, and a third of the night does too. That's a whole lot of dark to land on one clock.

That's it, baker. "When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour." The Lamb opens the seventh seal, and heaven goes quiet. I'd have checked whether my ears were still working.

Palm branches belong to Revelation 7:9, where a great multitude stands before the throne holding them. Here the text puts something else with the incense. It's the prayers of all the saints. The palm branches stay in the other scene.

True, and the text packs it in. When the censer is hurled to the earth, there are "…peals of thunder, rumblings, flashes of lightning, and an earthquake." That's sound, light and shaking in one list. I'd have grabbed the counter.

This one is true, friend. The text says that after the censer is hurled to the earth, "…there were peals of thunder, rumblings, flashes of lightning, and an earthquake." Nothing in that list gets skipped. Thunder, rumblings, lightning and an earthquake all show up.

Not this time, baker. The text says that after the second trumpet, a third of the sea turned to blood, and "…a third of the living creatures in the sea died…" So not every creature survives. This part is heavy, and the text just says it plainly.

The sun does stand still in the Bible, in Joshua 10:13, with Joshua, Israel's leader. That's a different story. Here the fourth angel sounds his trumpet, and a third of the sun and moon and stars were struck. A third of the day is without light, and a third of the night as well.
